column5: Purdue HO-327-W read in full confirms the figures the verification log listed as unchecked: forced ventilation of 8 to 10 cfm per square foot keeps air within about 5 F of outdoors; fans on the leeward side, clear space of 4 to 5 fan diameters, no more than 25 feet apart, add at least 10% capacity if not leeward; ridge plus sidewall vents beat either alone; insect screens cut natural ventilation by more than 50% in some studies; Indiana shade cloth cutting light by 30 to 50%.

Purdue HO-327-W temperature bands: most species grow best at 68 to 78 F (20 to 26 C); cold-tolerant species grow normally at 58 to 63 F (14 to 17 C); growth stops (plants survive) below a base temperature of 36 to 53 F (2 to 12 C); 78 to 85 F gives excess growth; above 90 F (32 C) heat damage such as leaf senescence or flower drop can occur.

Purdue HO-327-W light: keep a daily light integral of 10 to 12 moles per square metre for normal growth and 15 to 18 for vegetables such as tomatoes and peppers; an unshaded Indiana greenhouse can reach 20 to 25, which is why a 30 to 50% shade cloth still leaves enough light there. Gives the reason behind the course's shade figure; a UK greenhouse with less summer light may need less shade.

Purdue HO-327-W natural ventilation: side vents sit slightly above plant height; sidewall and roof vent areas should be similar and each about 15 to 20% of floor area; a ridge vent opened to about 60 degrees works best, while wider openings risk a 'sail effect' and vent failure in strong wind; do not run horizontal airflow fans while venting naturally, because they push the hot air at the roof back down.

Purdue HO-327-W heating: unvented heaters are more fuel-efficient but spread toxic combustion products to plants and people; heaters need an adequate air supply for complete combustion, a yearly check before the heating season (blower, fuel lines, valves, exhaust vent), and condensate from high-efficiency units is acidic and must not be used to water plants; cut losses first with heat curtains, double glazing, infrared-blocking film and foam in gaps.

Purdue HO-327-W root-zone heating: lettuce grew normally with heated nutrient solution at 70 F (21 C) while the air was held at 55 F (13 C), and was smaller with solution at 60 F; bench heating usually holds air about 10 F below optimal while warming the root zone, cutting heating cost.
